items.title: Close reading across a scriptural argument
items.body: A verse is part of a conversation, narrative, or argument. Before using it as evidence, identify who speaks, to whom, and in response to what. Notice repetition, contrast, and changes in audience. In a scriptural debate, an opponent’s words are not automatically the narrator’s endorsement. A reference chain can help, but a chain of isolated sentences can also conceal context. Practice by outlining an entire argument before choosing the few lines that support your thesis. Then state the strongest limitation on your interpretation. This makes your conclusion more useful, not weaker. The exercise assesses careful reading rather than your ability to attach many citations to an already fixed opinion.

items.title: Evidence, genre, and historical claim testing
items.body: Documents can support claims without supporting every claim made about them. A historical record may establish that a statement was made, while the truth of the statement requires a different argument. A sacred narrative can communicate theological meaning even when modern historical questions remain open. Avoid forcing one method to answer every question. Create an evidence table with columns for claim type, available evidence, alternative explanation, and conclusion strength. Distinguish absent evidence from evidence of absence, and a plausible possibility from a demonstrated event. Responsible scholarship also identifies the position of its sources. Institutional, devotional, and academic sources may all be useful, but they serve different purposes and should not be blended into an anonymous consensus.

items.title: Charity, disagreement, and pastoral case analysis
items.body: A well-argued position can still be expressed in a way that harms dialogue. Charity is not the avoidance of every disagreement; it includes how people are represented and treated while ideas are examined. In a pastoral case, ask what you know, what you are assuming, and what you are qualified to offer. A doctrinal explanation should not become an unearned diagnosis of a person’s motives, spiritual status, or mental health. Use fictional cases to practice attentive listening and source-based explanation. Preserve the person’s agency, acknowledge uncertainty, and identify when a trained professional or appropriate community leader is needed. The objective is a responsible response, not a script that promises to resolve every conflict.

items.title: Teaching responsibly and correcting mistakes
items.body: Teaching turns your interpretation into someone else’s starting point. A responsible lesson therefore makes its sources and limitations visible. Choose a learning objective that can actually be assessed, use enough context for the reader to evaluate a claim, and include an alternative interpretation when it is relevant. Avoid manufacturing certainty to make a lesson feel inspiring. When you discover an error, correct the content and explain the change plainly. A correction is part of scholarship rather than evidence that learning has failed. Accessibility also matters: a learner should be able to complete the objective without purchasing a book, watching an unavailable video, or disclosing private religious experiences. Build the lesson around understanding that can be demonstrated in several forms.

items.title: Capstone draft: discipleship and the public good
items.body: A theological synthesis should show why its ideas matter without claiming to solve every practical problem. Use a fictional ethical case to test your thesis. Identify the doctrine involved, the person’s needs, competing responsibilities, and the information you lack. Then explain a reasonable response and its limits. Do not turn religious teaching into unsourced legal, medical, or financial advice. In the draft, make the sequence of your argument visible: question, sources, interpretation, alternative, application, and limitations. Your reader should be able to follow each conclusion back to evidence. A practical section succeeds when it is both principled and realistic, including circumstances under which your recommendation would need to change.

items.title: Capstone revision and an ongoing scholar’s practice
items.body: Sage is a milestone in a learning path, not a certificate of religious authority. The final project demonstrates that you can integrate sources, reason fairly, and communicate responsibly. Ask a reviewer to identify the weakest claim, the least clear term, and the alternative you have represented least adequately. Revise those points before polishing the presentation. Provide an accessible summary for a newcomer and a transparent bibliography for a specialist. Keep an errata section and a list of questions for future study. Mature scholarship does not end with a tier badge: it continues through correction, better evidence, and more careful listening. The final assessment therefore values limitations and revision alongside accuracy and a coherent thesis.

capstone.title: A sourced LDS doctrinal synthesis
capstone.summary: Formats: 1,800–2,500-word essay; 20–30-minute presentation with written outline and source notes; Accessible equivalent approved against the same rubric
requirements: One bounded research question and a defensible thesis.
At least 10 substantively used sources, including at least 4 canonical selections and 2 current LDS institutional sources.

At least 1 historical primary source and 1 source representing a comparison tradition when relevant to the chosen question; otherwise explain why they are not relevant and substitute an appropriate academic or documentary source.
Identify perspective and claim type; do not treat an institutional essay as independent scholarly consensus.
One serious alternative reading or objection, answered or used to narrow the thesis.
One fictional practical or teaching application.
A claim-level citation trail, annotated bibliography, revision log, accessible newcomer summary, and at least 3 explicit limitations or open questions.
Use only original writing, approved app scripture rendering, links, and rights-cleared materials.

questions.prompt: A popular devotional author states a new theory of divine life. What evidence is needed before calling it official doctrine?
questions.guide: Identify commentary as commentary; consult appropriate canonical and current institutional sources; do not generalize from popularity.

questions.prompt: A passage is canonical, but a proposed interpretation is not explicitly stated in it. How should the claim be labeled?
questions.guide: Distinguish the authoritative text from the reader’s interpretation and give the reasoning and its limit.

questions.prompt: Why does a document’s date matter when describing current teaching?
questions.guide: It locates the claim historically; verify current teaching separately rather than assuming unchanged status.

questions.prompt: Give the four fields a beginner’s source ledger should contain.
questions.guide: Claim, source, setting, and confidence; equivalent fields are acceptable if they preserve attribution and limits.

questions.prompt: What topics appear in the first four Articles of Faith?
questions.guide: Godhead, individual accountability, Christ’s Atonement, and foundational principles and ordinances.

questions.prompt: What does D&C 130 distinguish about Father, Son, and Holy Ghost?
questions.guide: Father and Son have bodies; the Holy Ghost is a personage of spirit. State what is explicit without a complete metaphysical theory.

questions.prompt: Why is “unity” not necessarily equivalent to “the same person”?
questions.guide: Explain that a relationship of purpose or action can unite distinct persons; identify the meaning claimed by the source.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with using “God wearing three masks” as a definition of the Nicene Trinity?
questions.guide: It describes interchangeable appearances rather than the tradition’s distinct persons; avoid importing it as a fair comparison.

questions.prompt: Rewrite “Every Latter-day Saint believes exactly this” as a defensible source claim.
questions.guide: Use attributed language such as “This institutional source teaches…” and limit the claim to what the source supports.

questions.prompt: Can a learner earn course credit while disagreeing with a doctrine? Explain the assessment standard.
questions.guide: Yes; accurate explanation, evidence, and reasoning demonstrate learning. Assent or private spiritual experience is not assessed.

questions.prompt: What purpose does Moses 1:39 state?
questions.guide: God’s work and glory concern immortality and eternal life; distinguish purpose from complete chronology.

questions.prompt: Name six broad nodes in a plan-of-salvation learning diagram.
questions.guide: Creation, mortality, Christ’s redemption, resurrection, judgment, and eternal life; qualify the diagram as a model.

questions.prompt: Why should two uncertain details be marked on such a diagram?
questions.guide: It makes the boundary between textual statements and inference visible and prevents speculative detail from becoming certainty.

questions.prompt: How does Lehi connect moral agency with the Messiah?
questions.guide: Choice and freedom are described in relation to redemption rather than isolated self-sufficiency.

questions.prompt: Does agency mean that people choose all their circumstances?
questions.guide: No; moral action must be distinguished from control over circumstances and opportunity.

questions.prompt: What direction does repentance take in the doctrine of Christ?
questions.guide: It involves turning toward God in relation to faith in Christ, not merely reporting sadness.

questions.prompt: Name the foundational principles and ordinances in the path described by 2 Nephi 31.
questions.guide: Faith in Christ, repentance, baptism, receiving the Holy Ghost, and continuing steadfast discipleship.

questions.prompt: Why is baptism not the end of the path in this passage?
questions.guide: The passage calls for continuing faithfulness and endurance after entry.

questions.prompt: Distinguish a course checklist from a discipleship map.
questions.guide: One records assessable learning activities; the other depicts ongoing religious commitment that course XP cannot certify.

questions.prompt: What limit should a teacher observe when asking for evidence of learning?
questions.guide: Ask for explanation or analysis; do not require private confessions, testimony, or proof of spiritual worthiness.

questions.prompt: A friend asks whether a leader’s single remark is binding doctrine. Give a sourced response and two limits.
questions.guide: Distinguish statement and source type, consult appropriate institutional guidance, and avoid claiming a perfect hierarchy or universal member agreement.

questions.prompt: Explain the LDS Godhead to a Nicene reader without defining their belief as modalism.
questions.guide: State LDS distinctions and unity, use the other tradition’s own description, and distinguish terms.
questions.reference: Godhead; Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§232–267

questions.prompt: Create a short plan-of-salvation account that explicitly labels an inference.
questions.guide: Include divine purpose, Christ, mortality, and hope; separate textual statement from inferred detail.

questions.prompt: Explain why course completion and enduring discipleship are different kinds of progress.
questions.guide: Learning activities are assessable; conversion and private spiritual life cannot be certified by XP.

questions.prompt: Show how agency can coexist with unequal circumstances in a fictional case.
questions.guide: Distinguish moral response from control of circumstances and avoid blaming someone for every outcome.

questions.prompt: Why should Abraham 3 and Moses 4 first be read separately?
questions.guide: Their settings and emphases differ; a synthesis should follow contextual reading rather than impose a single chronology.

questions.prompt: What does a creation narrative’s theological purpose fail to establish by itself?
questions.guide: A scientific mechanism, date, or exhaustive physical history; those require evidence of another kind.

questions.prompt: Which aspects of suffering are addressed in Alma 7:11–13?
questions.guide: Suffering, infirmity, death, and sin in connection with Christ’s succoring role.

questions.prompt: What grounds redemption in 2 Nephi 2:6–9?
questions.guide: The Messiah and his sacrifice; distinguish the ground of redemption from human response.

questions.prompt: Why is a grace account incomplete if it portrays help as only a prize for previous achievement?
questions.guide: It obscures dependence on Christ; explain response and transformation without making self-sufficiency the basis.

questions.prompt: Name two communal responsibilities associated with baptism in Mosiah 18.
questions.guide: Any two of bearing burdens, mourning, comforting, witnessing, and covenant service, explained in context.

questions.prompt: Identify two commitments and a promised relationship in the sacrament prayers.
questions.guide: Remembrance and willingness to take Christ’s name or keep commandments, with the promised companionship of the Spirit.

questions.prompt: Why can D&C 8’s mind-and-heart language not be used as an infallible diagnosis of every feeling?
questions.guide: It is a revelatory instruction in context, not a universal mechanical test establishing every experience’s origin.

questions.prompt: What role does study play in D&C 9?
questions.guide: Preparation and inquiry precede asking in the translation setting; avoid guaranteeing identical experiences for every question.

questions.prompt: What is missing from a claim of personal revelation that directs another household?
questions.guide: Evidence of appropriate stewardship and respect for the other people’s agency; personal conviction alone does not supply authority.
questions.reference: A Framework for Personal Revelation — Dale G. Renlund

questions.prompt: Distinguish priesthood keys from a priesthood office.
questions.guide: Keys concern directing authorized work within responsibilities; an office is not an interchangeable term or measure of personal worth.

questions.prompt: What does D&C 121 offer as an alternative to coercive dominion?
questions.guide: Persuasion, patience, kindness, love, and related qualities; explain accountable service.

questions.prompt: What is an appropriate boundary for a public temple lesson?
questions.guide: Use publicly described purposes and covenants; do not reconstruct ceremonial details.

questions.prompt: Does proxy participation mean someone is compelled to accept an ordinance?
questions.guide: No; explain the LDS account of choice and distinguish the rite from compelled acceptance.

questions.prompt: How does D&C 128 connect generations?
questions.guide: Through an intergenerational relationship and linking imagery; do not make it a claim about forced outcomes.

questions.prompt: Distinguish resurrection from exaltation.
questions.guide: Resurrection concerns renewed life after death; exaltation concerns a fuller LDS account of eternal life and relationship with God.

questions.prompt: Why should D&C 76 not be used to assign a neighbor an eternal destination?
questions.guide: It describes theological categories, while the learner lacks authority and knowledge to judge individuals.

questions.prompt: What communal features define Zion in Moses 7:18?
questions.guide: Unity, righteousness, and absence of poverty, stated as the text’s ideal.

questions.prompt: How does Mosiah 4 complicate a service plan that shames people with limited resources?
questions.guide: It combines care for those in need with attention to circumstances; avoid equating limited resources with moral failure.

questions.prompt: Why does a religious ethic not by itself establish a complete public policy?
questions.guide: Policy also requires practical evidence, context, and expertise; distinguish principle from implementation.

questions.prompt: Explain grace and covenant responsibility using one redemption text and one baptism text.
questions.guide: Give contextual accounts without presenting human effort as independent salvation; connect communal responsibility.

questions.prompt: Respond to a fictional claim of authority enforced through intimidation.
questions.guide: Use D&C 121 to distinguish authorization from coercive dominion; explain accountable service.

questions.prompt: Explain temple work and agency to a newcomer using only public information.
questions.guide: Discuss public purposes and voluntary acceptance; avoid ceremonial reconstruction.

questions.prompt: Describe resurrection and eternal hope while refusing to assign someone’s final destiny.
questions.guide: Use relevant texts, distinguish terms, and explain the limit on individual judgment.

questions.prompt: Turn a Zion principle into a realistic hypothetical service proposal.
questions.guide: State the principle, participant needs, resource limits, and practical evidence needed.

questions.prompt: What must a fair LDS–Nicene comparison do with “person” and “unity”?
questions.guide: Define each tradition’s terms from its own sources and acknowledge that they do not map exactly.
questions.reference: Godhead; Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§232–267

questions.prompt: What question is central to the Nicene clauses about the Son’s relation to the Father?
questions.guide: The Son’s divine relation and nature; answer from the creed rather than substituting LDS definitions.
questions.reference: The Nicene Creed — The Orthodox Faith

questions.prompt: Why does John 17 alone not settle all later metaphysical disagreements?
questions.guide: Its prayer context supplies relational and unity language, but later systems involve additional interpretation and commitments.

questions.prompt: How do Augsburg Articles IV and VI relate justification and obedience?
questions.guide: Distinguish justification from the expected good works of living faith; do not claim Lutheranism rejects moral action.
questions.reference: Augsburg Confession, Articles IV and VI

questions.prompt: Why read Ephesians 2:10 with 2:8–9?
questions.guide: It places good works alongside gift language, preventing an incomplete excerpt-based contrast.

questions.prompt: What claim about faith does James 2 interrogate?
questions.guide: Faith claimed without practical action or care; identify its argument rather than a slogan.

questions.prompt: Distinguish open canon from the claim that every new opinion is scripture.
questions.guide: Continuing revelation does not automatically confer canonical status on every individual interpretation.

questions.prompt: What dates must be distinguished when discussing a First Vision account?
questions.guide: The reported event date and the date of the written record, along with its setting and audience.

questions.prompt: Why is a shared phrase about divine participation insufficient to establish identical theologies?
questions.guide: Terms operate within different systems; the comparison requires contextual sources and an account of differences.

questions.prompt: How would reciprocal conscience reasoning apply to a town rule?
questions.guide: Evaluate the rule with majority and minority positions reversed, including nonbelievers; separate theology from legal advice.

questions.prompt: What four details should accompany a claim about doctrinal change?
questions.guide: Exact claim, date, source type, and meaning of change; avoid an all-or-nothing slogan.

questions.prompt: How does D&C 1’s human-language framing discipline interpretation?
questions.guide: It invites attention to language, weakness, correction, and learning without supplying the same explanation for every change.

questions.prompt: Why is “plural marriage ended everywhere immediately in 1890” inaccurate?
questions.guide: Distinguish the declaration from subsequent institutional transitions and documented practice.
questions.reference: The Manifesto and the End of Plural Marriage

questions.prompt: What source limitation must a history of plural marriage acknowledge?
questions.guide: Uneven documentation and underrepresented perspectives; absence of a record does not settle consent or experience.
questions.reference: Plural Marriage in Kirtland and Nauvoo

questions.prompt: What groups were affected by the historical priesthood and temple restrictions?
questions.guide: Black men faced priesthood restrictions, and Black men and women faced temple restrictions; specify the scope accurately.

questions.prompt: How should a contemporary explanation treat disavowed racial theories?
questions.guide: Identify them as rejected explanations, not established doctrine or facts.

questions.prompt: Why does a historical account of women’s participation not automatically settle a current policy?
questions.guide: Dates, source type, development, and current institutional guidance must be distinguished.
questions.reference: Joseph Smith’s Teachings about Priesthood, Temple, and Women

questions.prompt: How should a family lesson treat learners with differing circumstances?
questions.guide: Explain the source accurately, recognize circumstances, and avoid grading family status or personal assent.
questions.reference: The Family: A Proclamation to the World

questions.prompt: What is the appropriate response when an affirmed teaching leaves many details unstated?
questions.guide: Separate affirmation from interpretation and speculation; record open questions instead of inventing answers.

questions.prompt: What should happen to an untraceable quotation central to an argument?
questions.guide: Locate its source or label it unverified and avoid resting a major claim on it.

questions.prompt: Compare an LDS teaching with a Catholic or Lutheran source, identifying a genuine difference.
questions.guide: Represent each accurately, define terms, and do not generalize one confession to all Christianity.
questions.reference: Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§232–267; Augsburg Confession, Articles IV and VI

questions.prompt: Separate a restoration claim into documentary, confessional, and interpretive elements.
questions.guide: Identify evidence appropriate to each element and avoid labeling faith claims scholarly consensus.

questions.prompt: Explain why a historical declaration and the end of a practice may have different dates.
questions.guide: Distinguish document, institutional transition, and evidence of practice; use the plural-marriage chronology accurately.
questions.reference: The Manifesto and the End of Plural Marriage

questions.prompt: Write a concise, humane account of racial restrictions that distinguishes past claims from current teaching.
questions.guide: Identify exclusion and its scope, the 1978 end, and repudiated explanations without repeating them as truth.

questions.prompt: Present an open theological question with one established claim and one unsupported speculation.
questions.guide: Identify the source boundary and refuse to present attractive conjecture as settled knowledge.

questions.prompt: Why should a reader outline Alma 32 before extracting a line about faith?
questions.guide: The audience, argument, and growth analogy supply meaning that an isolated line can lose.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between documenting a statement and proving its truth?
questions.guide: A document can establish that a claim was made; its truth may require different evidence or theological commitments.

questions.prompt: What is required before claiming scholarly consensus?
questions.guide: Identify the field, representative scholarship, relevant date, and actual agreement; one institutional source is insufficient.

questions.prompt: What makes a labeled concept-map arrow better than a bare line?
questions.guide: It states a defensible relationship that can be tested against sources.

questions.prompt: How should an unresolved tension appear in a synthesis?
questions.guide: State it clearly, retain the difficult evidence, and identify a next interpretive step rather than hide it.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between explaining disagreement and producing contention?
questions.guide: Represent the idea accurately and reason about it without contempt or personal coercion.

questions.prompt: Does a teaching on forgiveness eliminate safety boundaries or accountability?
questions.guide: No; do not infer permission for continued harm or silencing reports from the teaching.

questions.prompt: What learning evidence can replace a required unavailable video?
questions.guide: An equivalent original accessible lesson and task that demonstrates the same objective; provider availability is not a learning prerequisite.

questions.prompt: What should an error correction note include?
questions.guide: The original error, corrected claim, source, and affected materials; explain the change plainly.

questions.prompt: Why is a teacher’s source transparency part of responsible instruction?
questions.guide: It lets learners check claims, context, and limits rather than relying entirely on the teacher’s confidence.

questions.prompt: What makes a capstone question researchable?
questions.guide: Defined scope, intended audience, available evidence, and a claim that can be revised; avoid trying to explain all doctrine.

questions.prompt: What should a source annotation explain beyond the title and URL?
questions.guide: Perspective, setting, contribution to the claim, rights status, and an interpretive limit.

questions.prompt: Why is a strong counterargument useful?
questions.guide: It tests evidence and may improve or narrow the thesis; a caricature cannot perform that function.

questions.prompt: How does Philippians 2:12–13 complicate a simple action-versus-grace contrast?
questions.guide: Read human action with God’s working rather than isolating one verse.

questions.prompt: What caution applies when synthesizing judgment passages?
questions.guide: Read each in context and avoid declaring individual outcomes or erasing their differing questions.

questions.prompt: Why should Revelation 21 not be treated as a literal architectural plan?
questions.guide: It is visionary imagery communicating renewal and divine presence; distinguish genre and proposed inference.

questions.prompt: What should a Sabbath or Word of Wisdom explanation distinguish?
questions.guide: Scriptural purpose and instructions, subsequent institutional application, and unsupported universal or medical guarantees.
questions.reference: Doctrine and Covenants 59:9–13; Doctrine and Covenants 89:18–21

questions.prompt: How does the Good Samaritan narrative test an abstract account of neighbor-love?
questions.guide: It moves attention to enacted mercy and challenges category boundaries.

questions.prompt: What belongs in a revision log?
questions.guide: Initial claim, critique, change or reasoned retention, and supporting evidence.

questions.prompt: What does Sage certify and what does it not certify?
questions.guide: Successful learning milestones and synthesis; it does not confer religious office, spiritual rank, or scholarly consensus authority.

questions.prompt: Audit a capstone paragraph that combines source claims and the writer’s interpretation.
questions.guide: Mark claim types, supply missing citations, qualify conclusions, and separate interpretation from attributed facts.

questions.prompt: Reconstruct a serious alternative reading before defending your own.
questions.guide: Explain its actual evidence and implications; answer or narrow the thesis without a straw man.

questions.prompt: Apply a doctrinal synthesis to a fictional ethical case and identify a professional boundary.
questions.guide: Use sourced principles, attend to circumstances and agency, and identify information or expertise needed.

questions.prompt: Design an accessible lesson that remains completable if an external video disappears.
questions.guide: Provide an original equivalent objective and task, avoid duplicate XP, and maintain a source trail.

questions.prompt: Show how a reviewer’s objection changed your conclusion.
questions.guide: Provide before-and-after claims, evidence, revision rationale, and a remaining limitation.
